subject: Hosted→Dedicated migration: Sentinel-Concord capacity attestation & cutover matrix
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha@sentinel.ai>, Mike Lawson <mike.lawson@concordhealth.io>
Cc: ops+procurement@sentinel.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Sentinel-Concord migration — capacity attestation framework and next steps

Hi Asha / Mike,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion I attached a first-pass capacity model and a compact cutover matrix so your infra and procurement teams can validate assumptions. High-level notes: 

- Model is traffic-driven: uses 95th percentile token/s request rates you shared (peak: 2.6M tokens/min, 95th sustained: 1.2M tokens/min) and our profiling from the same model under 4x quantized runtime.
- We proposed a dedicated pool size of 12 inference GPUs (A100-80GB equivalent) for a conservative committed baseline, with burst lanes for traffic spikes.
- Cutover matrix includes a 48-hour staging rehearsal, a 2-hour blackout window for the swap, and an immediate fallback to hosted for the first 72 hours.

Ask for Sentinel/Concord: please confirm the following by EOD Thu so we can finalize resource reservations for your Nov onboarding sprint: 
1) Accept/adjust peak and sustained RPS assumptions (cells highlighted).
2) Confirm procurement lead and preferred DocuSign contact for the reserved capacity amendment.
3) Indicate any compliance controls (e.g., IP allowlists / private VPC subnets) that would affect the staging plan.

Attachments: sentinel_capacity_model_v1.xlsx (breakdown), cutover_matrix_draft.pdf (timeline + gates)

I'll loop in our Delivery leads once I have your confirmation.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0172
From: Mike Lawson <mike.lawson@concordhealth.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Asha Patel <asha@sentinel.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sentinel-Concord migration — capacity attestation framework and next steps

Karthik — thanks for the doc. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- Peak numbers look right; the 95th sustained figures are slightly conservative for our September traffic but they’re OK to use for the baseline.
- For procurement: cc'ing our vendor ops alias (vendorops@concordhealth.io) — they'll handle the paperwork and PO.
- Compliance: we need private subnetting and customer-managed KMS. I attached a short checklist (sent separately to procurement).

Two blockers before we can commit: 
1) A short SLA addendum for latency SLOs at the committed baseline — our security/compliance wants explicit p99 latency targets.
2) A short service window preference: prefer swap during our maintenance window (Sun 02:00–06:00 local).

If we can get SLA language and the final pricing, procurement can move fast.

—Mike
Director, Platform Engineering | Concord Health
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Sentinel-Concord migration — capacity attestation framework and next steps

Team — forwarding Concord's reply. Two asks from procurement/security: p99 latency SLO at baseline, private subnet + customer-managed KMS, and a Sunday early-morning swap preference. Need quick alignment so we can lock the reserved pool for Nov.

Proposed internal plan (short):
- SLA: Offer a 99th/95th p99 latency target for baseline traffic profile; include a remediation credit schedule (small % applied per 15m window) — keep it narrow to avoid open-ended obligations.
- Staging: 48h smoke in our staging region, then a live swap in customer's maintenance window with 72h fallback to hosted.
- Fleet: 12 committed GPUs, 4 burst GPUs available for 2x traffic spikes.

Monica — can Delivery validate we can guarantee the p99 number on the proposed stack (4x quantized model path) for Concord's 95th sustained? Ben — need cost delta for 12 base + 4 burst vs 10 base + 6 burst. Marissa — prep an SLA clause draft (one pager) we can share with legal. Grace — can you check KMS onboarding timeline with our security partners?

I want a short internal sync today at 4pm PT to finalize language.

Thanks,
Karthik

Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sentinel-Concord migration — capacity attestation framework and next steps

Karthik / team — I ran the capacity model through our staging profiles. Summary:

- For Concord's 95th sustained load the 4x quantized path holds p99 latency under 380ms in our staging environment with the proposed 12-GPU pool. This meets the suggested p99 objective with ~15% headroom.
- The burst lanes (4 GPUs) can absorb short 2x spikes for up to ~18 minutes before we see queue growth; we should model longer spikes with incremental autoscale.
- Risk: if Concord enables long-running streaming sessions (avg session length > 90s) the KV cache pressure increases and p99 may rise ~20–30% — recommend session length guardrails or adaptive cache sizing.

Action items from Delivery:
- I'll export the test logs and attach the heatmap to the Drive link.
- Recommend we capture the p99 guarantee as conditional on the traffic profile and session-length guardrails.

I'll be on the 4pm sync.

—Monica
Senior Delivery Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Sentinel-Concord migration — capacity attestation framework and next steps

Draft SLA clause (attached as text below) — feel free to refine for legal.

--- SLA DRAFT ---
Redwood will maintain a p99 inference latency of <= 400ms for the committed baseline during Concord Health's 95th percentile traffic profile as defined in Attachment A (traffic matrix). This SLA is conditional on: (a) ingress patterns remain within the described session-length and RPS profiles, (b) customer uses the agreed quantized model variant, and (c) customer provides a private subnet and KMS integration per onboarding checklist. 
Remedy: For any monthly aggregate period where p99 latency exceeds the target in 3 or more non-overlapping 15-minute windows, Redwood will issue a service credit equal to 2% of that month's reserved capacity fee per additional occurrence, up to a maximum of 10%.
--- end SLA DRAFT ---

I'll drop this into the DocuSign package and mark the SLA as an addendum to the reserved capacity contract.

—Marissa
Principal Contracts Manager | Redwood Inference
